'''Joël Scherk''' ({{IPA|fr|jɔɛl ʃɛʁk|lang}}; 27 May 1946 – 16 May 1980) was a French theoretical [[physicist]] who studied [[string theory]] and [[supergravity]].<ref>[[INSPIRE-HEP]] [http://inspirehep.net/search?p=find+author+joel+scherk List of Joël Scherk's scientific publications]</ref>

==Education==
Scherk studied in Paris at the [[École Normale Supérieure]] (ENS). In 1969 he received his diploma (Thèse de troisième cycle) at [[University of Paris XI]] in Orsay with {{Ill|Philippe Meyer (physicist)|lt=Philippe Meyer|fr|Philippe Meyer (physicien)}} and [[Claude Bouchiat]] and in 1971 he completed his doctorate ([[Doctorat d'État]]) at the same time as his colleague [[André Neveu]].<ref>{{cite book|last=Schwarz|first=John H.|chapter=The scientific contributions of Joël Scherk|date=2012|chapter-url=https://www.cambridge.org/core/product/identifier/CBO9780511977725A095/type/book_part|title=The Birth of String Theory|pages=496–508|editor-last=Cappelli|editor-first=Andrea|place=Cambridge|publisher=Cambridge University Press|doi=10.1017/cbo9780511977725.045|isbn=978-0-511-97772-5|s2cid=17286558 |access-date=2021-07-23|editor2-last=Castellani|editor2-first=Elena|editor3-last=Colomo|editor3-first=Filippo|editor4-last=Di Vecchia|editor4-first=Paolo|arxiv=0904.0537}}</ref>

== Career ==
In 1974, together with [[John H. Schwarz]], Scherk discovered that the [[Veneziano amplitude]] would have a massless spin-2 particle hypothesized as the [[graviton]], soon it was realised that string theory was a theory of [[quantum gravity]]. In 1978, together with [[Eugène Cremmer]] and [[Bernard Julia]], Scherk constructed the [[Lagrangian (field theory)|Lagrangian]] and [[supersymmetry]] transformations for [[eleven-dimensional supergravity]],<ref>{{cite journal | last1=Cremmer | first1=E. | last2=Julia | first2=B. | last3=Scherk | first3=J. | title=Supergravity in theory in 11 dimensions | journal=Physics Letters B | publisher=Elsevier BV | volume=76 | issue=4 | year=1978 | issn=0370-2693 | doi=10.1016/0370-2693(78)90894-8 | pages=409–412| bibcode=1978PhLB...76..409C}} [https://lib-extopc.kek.jp/preprints/PDF/1978/7805/7805106.pdf Preprint scanned document], LPTENS-78-10. {{retrieved|access-date=20 December 2025|via=[[KEK]]}}</ref> which is one of the foundations of [[M-theory]].

== Death ==
He died unexpectedly, and in tragic circumstances, months after the supergravity workshop at the [[State University of New York at Stony Brook]] that was held on 27–29 September 1979. The workshop proceedings were dedicated to his memory, with a statement that Scherk, a [[diabetic]], had been trapped somewhere without his [[insulin]] and went into a [[diabetic coma]].<ref>{{cite book |title=Supergravity: proceedings of the Supergravity workshop at Stony Brook, 27-29 September 1979 |editor1-last=Nieuwenhuizen |editor1-first=Peter van |editor1-link=Peter van Nieuwenhuizen |editor2-last=Freedman |editor2-first=Daniel Z. |editor2-link=Daniel Z. Freedman |location=Amsterdam |publisher=North-Holland |year=1979 |isbn=0-444-85438-X |url=https://archive.org/details/supergravityproc0000supe |url-access=registration |access-date=20 December 2025 |via=Internet Archive}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book |last=Hawking |first=Stephen |author-link=Stephen Hawking |title=A brief history of time: from the big bang to black holes |date=2016 |publisher=Bantam Books |isbn=978-0-85750-100-4 |edition=Bantam edition reissued |location=London |pages=195}}</ref>

== Legacy ==
Two decades later, in his 2001 book ''Euclid's Window'', author and theoretical physicist [[Leonard Mlodinow]] credited Schwarz and Scherk for their "astounding discovery" that gravity was part of string theory in a way that would "avoid contradictions between general relativity and quantum mechanics", but noted that Scherk suffered a [[mental breakdown|breakdown]], his wife left with their children, and he later committed [[suicide]].<ref>{{cite book |title=Euclid's Window: The Story of Geometry from Parallel Lines to Hyperspace |first=Leonard |last=Mlodinow |author-link=Leonard Mlodinow |publisher=Touchstone/Simon & Schuster |location=New York |year=2001 |edition=Touchstone 2002 |isbn=0-684-86523-8 |page=251-252 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=GHY6VM3NsIwC&q=Jo%C3%ABl+Scherk |access-date=2020-12-06 |via=[[Google Books]]}}</ref>

The high-energy theory library of the Laboratoire de Physique Théorique at École Normale Supérieure (Paris) is dedicated in his honor. A [[Academic conference|conference]] in Paris, on 16–20 October 2006, celebrating 30 years of supergravity,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://string.lpthe.jussieu.fr/sugra30/index.html |title=30 Years of Supergravity |date=31 July 2006 |access-date=20 December 2025}}</ref> was dedicated to Scherk.
